provenance.locator: Employee Compensation > Stock Options > Statutory Stock Options > Employee stock purchase plan > Holding period requirement not satisfied > Example 11 (incorporates Example 10)
provenance.quote: The facts are the same as in Example 10, except that you sold the stock only 6 months after you exercised the option. You didn’t satisfy the holding period requirement, so you must report $300 as wages and $700 as capital gain, figured as follows.
provenance.original_timing: 18 months from grant to exercise (Example 10); 6 months from exercise to sale. No calendar years given.
provenance.adaptation: Calendar dates assigned to place the sale in 2025, preserving both intervals. Shares 100, cost $20, grant FMV $22, exercise FMV $23, sale price $30, wages $300 and capital gain $700 retain original IRS amounts. Zero fees, reported basis of purchase cost, unrestricted unadjusted shares, complete disposal history and arm's-length FMV sale are fixture assumptions.

sources.locator: Statutory Stock Options, Employee stock purchase plan, Examples 10 and 11
